citation.title: Test and Analysis of a Buckling-Critical Large-Scale Sandwich Composite Cylinder
citation.authors: M. R. Schultz, D. W. Sleight, N. W. Gardner, M. T. Rudd, M. W. Hilburger, T. E. Palm, N. J. Oldfield
citation.venue: 2018 AIAA SciTech Forum, Kissimmee FL (AIAA paper); NTRS report number NF1676L-27252
citation.doi: 10.2514/6.2018-1693 (not on the paper's own NTRS page; seen in the reference list of NASA/TM-20205008667 p.60, ref 12)

what_i_could_read: full text (PDF via pdftotext, 18 pp, incl. Table 1, Table 2 rendered and checked as image)

shell.loading: pure axial compression to failure (final load case); earlier subcritical cases included compression plus bending
shell.boundary: aluminum pi-section end rings, potted in epoxy grout; ring settling observed in test, not modeled

geometry.R_note: derived by halving the stated 8-ft diameter (unit conversion only); R not printed
geometry.L_note: barrel shortened by 20 in. after FWD padup repair; test section 80.4 in (DIC)

faces.material: Cytec IM7/MTM45 unidirectional prepreg, 145 gsm, out-of-autoclave
faces.t_f_note: face thickness not stated as one number. Nominal ply 0.0052 in; posttest measured average ply 0.005679 in (9.2% thicker than nominal) x 7 plies. Not multiplied here.

pretest_modified.note: E1,E2 raised 8.71% to match subcritical axial stiffness

faces.E_f_note: laminate stiffness not tabulated; lamina values above. IM7/MTM45 properties were NOT available; IM7/8552 used as generic.

core.type: honeycomb (Hexcel KOREX, designation KOREX-1/8-4.5), ribbon direction axially aligned
core.density: designation '4.5'; Table 1 mass density 6.729e-6 lb-s^2/in^4 (as printed, not converted)

G_c_psi.direction_note: text does not say which of G13/G23 is axial-transverse; ribbon axial. Pretest material tests failed, so core values are 'assumed and vendor-provided'.

measured.kN_stated_elsewhere: 3811 kN in Uriol Balbin 2025 thesis Table 6.4 (same test; unit check only)
measured.mode: sudden global buckling; strength failure followed (stability failure first: ~5,200 microstrain at initiation vs 8,400 average failure strain in coupons)

predicted.what: pretest nonlinear FE (Abaqus S4R shell elements, measured radial imperfection + core-thickness variation, E1/E2 recalibrated, entire test assembly)
posttest nonlinear FE with nonlinear fiber-direction stiffness
perfect-shell linear eigenvalue load
predicted.note: value not stated in this paper; only the ratio 0.87 is given (test / perfect eigenvalue)

predicted.what: closed-form Reese-Bert type (includes core transverse shear compliance, no padups), from NASA/TM-20205008667 Table 2
predicted.note: cross-source; for the idealized CTA8.1 design, not for as-tested 100 in barrel; ratio to test not stated in either source

transverse_shear_in_prediction: not stated for the S4R model in this paper (core modeled as a layer with G13, G23 per Table 1); closed-form in TM-20205008667 does include it
recommended_kdf: none recommended; authors say 0.87 is 'not to be used as a design recommendation'. SP-8007 orthotropic KDF calculated for this article = 0.61

quotes.quote: 8-ft-diameter, 120-in.-long honeycomb-core sandwich composite cylinder
the axially stiff 7-ply facesheets had a total layup of [45/-45/0/90/0/-45/45]T
predicted buckling load of 864,600 lb and measured buckling load of 856,900
The orthotropic SP-8007 KDF calculated for CTA8.1 is 0.61
normalized buckling load (test buckling load divided by predicted perfect eigenvalue bucking load) was 0.87

gaps: R, t_f (single value), laminate E_f and perfect eigenvalue load not stated
G13 vs G23 direction mapping not stated
SP-8007 does not cover sandwich composite cylinders (stated p.7); 0.61 is the orthotropic-cylinder KDF

citation.title: Buckling Test and Analysis of the 8-Foot-Diameter Sandwich Composite Cylinder Test Article CTA8.2 as Part of the Shell Buckling Knockdown Factor Project: Test Dates 5-7 December 2017

what_i_could_read: full text (PDF via pdftotext; figures not viewed)

shell.loading: uniform axial compression (LS8); one planned load-to-failure sequence
shell.boundary: aluminum pi-section attachment rings, potted, release agent applied (sliding-type axial condition modeled)

faces.material: Hexcel IM7/8552-1, 190 gsm, autoclave, automated fiber placement
faces.t_f_note: TM-20210024095 gives no ply thickness. TM-20205008667 Table 4 lists 0.00694 in cured ply for the 190 gsm material (that report says it applied to CTA8.2B; same 190 gsm material is named here).

core.type: aluminum honeycomb Hexcel 3.1-1/8-0.0007N-5056 (3.1 pcf); heavier 8.1 pcf core NOT used in CTA8.2

G_c_psi.direction_note: TM-20205008667 nomenclature defines G13, G23 as axial and circumferential transverse shear moduli

measured.mode: NOT global buckling: core damage (transverse shear + through-thickness crush) in padup region near the FWD attachment ring initiated failure; article failed before developing global buckling

predicted.what: linear eigenvalue (Lanczos), perfect geometry, with attachment rings, nominal properties
nonlinear transient FE with as-manufactured radial+thickness imperfections, entire apparatus (Abaqus S4R)
predicted.ratio_stated: test = 81.9% of predicted global buckling load

predicted.what: nonlinear FE, perfect geometry
closed form, Reese and Bert (transverse shear compliance in core included, in-plane core stiffness neglected), no padups

transverse_shear_in_prediction: closed form: yes (Appendix B, Eq. B1). Shell FE: core modeled as layer in S4R; transverse-shear treatment not stated in text.
ratio_as_stated: 708.1 kips = 77.5% Pcr (linear eigenvalue); 81.9% of nonlinear imperfect prediction
recommended_kdf_note: no KDF recommended and no SP-8007 KDF stated in this report

quotes.quote: layup of [±60/0]s and the core was 0.20 in. thick
was 913,920 lbf and was obtained using a Lanczos eigenanalysis
the test article failed at a load of 708.1 kips
The test article failed at 708 kips, before developing global buckling
significant core damage consistent with both transverse shearing
The predicted buckling load using the perfect-geometry transient nonlinear FEA was 984 kips
which considers transverse shear compliance in the core, but neglects the in-plane core stiffness
slightly higher than 973 kips predicted by the closed-form solution

gaps: t_f and G_c not in this report (taken from TM-20205008667, flagged)
NOT a clean buckling datum: collapse by core failure at end-ring region at 77.5% of linear Pcr; 8.2 was designed for 8.2B/8.3 changes (8.1 pcf end core) after this test per TM-20210024768 p.12

predicted.ratio_stated: test = 72.1% of linear buckling combined load (27.9% reduction)

predicted.what: nonlinear FE, as-manufactured imperfections, LS12
nonlinear FE, as-installed radial midsurface + as-manufactured thickness imperfections, LS12

quotes.quote: The 8-ft diameter, 100-in. long test article CTA8.2B

what_i_could_read: full text (PDF via pdftotext). Pretest design report: NO test results; used here for lamina and core properties and closed-form predictions that the test reports reference.

3.1pcf.unit_note: E11, E22, G12 values printed as 5.8, 2.9, 1.45 under 'psi' heading (likely a unit slip in source; not corrected)

core.G_direction: G13, G23 = transverse shear moduli in the axial and circumferential directions (nomenclature, p.xi)

predicted.what: closed form (Reese-Bert with core shear compliance), perfect, Table 2 / Table 7
eigenvalue FE, perfect (Table 7)
nonlinear transient FE, imperfect (Table 7)

ratio_as_stated: closed-form vs eigenvalue FE differ by at most 4.3% (CTA8.5), average 2.7%
note_not_a_buckling_kdf: Appendix E defines a CO-CURE knockdown factor of 0.71 on sandwich facesheet properties (literature range 0.50-0.75); it is a material strength factor, not a shell-buckling KDF.

quotes.quote: typical knockdown factor for comparable sandwich composites was determined to be between 0.50 and 0.75

gaps: CTA8.4 and CTA8.5 appear only as designs; TM-20210024081 calls CTA8.2B 'the fourth and final composite test article' so I found no test for 8.4/8.5

what_i_could_read: full text; the relevant pages (46, 48, 50) were also rendered and viewed as images; Figure 4-13 is a curve with no table, so its values are only visual

statement.scope: isotropic sandwich cylinders only; no recommendations for sandwich composite cylinders
statement.axial_compression: KDF gamma uses the orthotropic Eq. 60 form, gamma = 1 - 0.901(1 - exp(-phi)), with phi = (sqrt(2)/29.8)*sqrt(r/h) where r is radius and h the depth between facesheet centroids (nomenclature: h = depth between centroids); plotted as Figure 4-13 vs r/h (curve starts near 0.87 at r/h=10 and falls to near 0.3 at r/h=1000, by eye). Transverse shear enters only the classical buckling load (Figs 4-11, 4-12), not gamma.
statement.lateral_pressure: no experimental data substantiate the pressure coefficients; gamma = 0.56 suggested from isotropic-cylinder experience (p.50)
statement.core_limit: designs limited to honeycomb density ratio delta > 0.03 unless substantiated by tests (axial, bending, pressure, torsion)
statement.empirical_basis: for isotropic sandwich the KDF is a modified isotropic-cylinder lower bound, based on 'two analytical investigations' not sandwich tests
statement.modern_test_remark: it is not uncommon to obtain experimental buckling loads of 70-90% of theoretical for uniform composite cylinders (stated for layered/unstiffened orthotropic cylinders)

quotes.quote: This knockdown factor is based Eq. 60,
recommendation is to use a modified version of the empirical knockdown factors
There are no experimental data to substantiate Figure 4-15
suggests that a knockdown factor 𝛾 = 0.56 should be used with this configuration
buckling loads for uniform cylinders of 70−90% of the theoretical predictions
𝛿 > 0.03, unless the design is substantiated by tests

gaps: Figure 4-13 numeric values not tabulated; only Eq. 115 + Eq. 60 are exact
density-ratio definition (delta) not checked beyond nomenclature line 'ratio of honeycomb core density to facesheet density'

statement.transverse_shear: extra caution for cylinders with low transverse shear stiffness (some sandwich shells): predicted buckling loads significantly lower than for high-shear-stiffness shells
statement.basis: nonlinear FE (analysis), no test numbers in the bulletin

quotes.quote: the universal KDF of 0.65 is thought to be unconservative for certain designs
suggests that these SP-8007 KDFs are conservative for all the sandwich composite cylinders considered
cylindrical shells with low transverse shear stiffness (such as some sandwich shells)

citation.title: Buckling Design and Imperfection Sensitivity of Sandwich Composite Launch-Vehicle Shell Structures
citation.authors: M. R. Schultz, D. W. Sleight, D. E. Myers, W. A. Waters Jr., P. B. Chunchu, A. E. Lovejoy, M. W. Hilburger
citation.venue: conference paper (NTRS date 19 Sep 2016; the PDF's own cover template points to the ASC2016 conference; venue not named on the NTRS page)

statement.type: numerical study, NO buckling test; optimized honeycomb sandwich designs (Ares V Intertank, Interstage, SLS Upper Stage Skirt, SLS Interstage) with the measured imperfection shape of a 13-ft fluted-core composite barrel scaled in

quotes.quote: the normalized buckling loads are greater than 0.8 for all cases
More work needs to be completed before actual recommendations can be made
the SP-8007 knockdown factor recommendation is the lowest normalized buckling load

gaps: analysis only, not measured; transverse-shear treatment of its FE models not checked
